note: Three Upgrade Roadmap 2 animal-feed systems. Existing workbook numbers are unchanged. Reference quantities and game assumptions are distinguished in row notes.

resources.name: Feed storage
resources.note: Dedicated hay/feed volume; joins the LL-33 feed pool without providing tool storage.

systems.name: Hay Meadow (1/10 acre)
systems.description: Grow and cut dryland hay; a working scythe reduces cutting labor without raising the land yield.
systems.notes: About 200 lb hay/year on 0.1 acre: within CSU dryland grass hay range 0.5-1.5 tons/acre. https://boulder.extension.colostate.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2021/03/BoCo-Rural-Living-Guide-Agriculture-Rev-1.pdf ; footprint uses 4,356 sq ft, output follows the growing season and drought. Total Labor 0.3 h/week includes 0.1 h upkeep and 0.2 h cutting; LL-34 scythe speeds cutting only. Costs, labor, mix ratios, loss and usable storage are experimental game balance.

systems.name: Poultry Feed Mix
systems.description: Mix grain, green biomass and grubs into stored chicken feed.
systems.notes: 7 lb Grain + 2 lb Green biomass + 1 lb Grubs -> 9 lb Chicken feed per week; 1 lb processing loss. All three ingredients are required. Nutrient balancing is abstracted; not a poultry ration recommendation. https://extension.umn.edu/agriculture/animals-and-livestock/poultry/raising-chickens-for-eggs Costs, labor, mix ratios, loss and usable storage are experimental game balance.

systems.name: Hay Barn
systems.description: Covered, dedicated storage for hay and poultry feed.
systems.notes: 200 cu ft usable storage shared by Hay and Chicken feed. Existing LL-33 densities apply: 9.5 lb hay/cu ft and 40 lb feed/cu ft, so mixed stocks use the same room. Provides no tool storage. Storage rationale: https://extension.psu.edu/how-much-does-that-bale-really-weigh-feeding-and-fertilizer-implications Costs, labor, mix ratios, loss and usable storage are experimental game balance.
